source: Mikro, DPM680 Modbus Communication Manual (firmware version 2.0), list of registers, tables 2 to 6

sources.title: Modbus 680 DPM Power Meter Communication Manual
sources.note: Register tables for device and communication info, operations data, power factor, harmonics and settings. The user manual (chapter 5) refers to this document.

notes: Modbus RTU on RS-485 or Modbus TCP/IP (DPM680 only; the device ID is fixed at 1 for TCP). The addresses are the same for both. All registers can be read with function 03 or 04; only the settings registers can be written, with function 06, and only after that is enabled on the meter's touch buttons. Serial parameters are set on the meter (parity and baud rate registers are listed).

The manual lists register numbers from 0 (device info 0000 to 0007, communication 1000 upward, operations from 4000, settings from 100); they are used as printed, address base 0. All registers are listed as holding registers (function 03; function 04 reads the same data).

Registers are 16-bit words; the manual says multi-register values follow the big-endian convention unless otherwise stated, so the high word comes first. 'byte' values (device ID, parity, baud rate, power factor sectors, harmonics, sub intervals) occupy one register and the upper bits are to be ignored; they are mapped as uint16. 'dword' is unsigned 32-bit, 'int' signed 32-bit, 'long' signed 64-bit; negative numbers are two's complement.
Time stamps are BCD words (year and month, day and hour, minute and second); they are listed as raw uint16 values, with the digit layout in the description.

Left out: the device info registers 0000 to 0007 (device type and version number), whose type and range are not clear from the table. The settings table in the manual ends at register 113 (registers 108 to 110 are not listed). Power factor, THD and power-factor-sector registers return 0xFFFF when the value is indeterminate.
Written from the manufacturer's manual; not tested on a device.

registers.name: Parity selection
registers.description: 0 = none, 1 stop bit; 1 = none, 2 stop bits; 2 = odd, 1 stop bit; 3 = even, 1 stop bit

registers.name: IP address
registers.description: Four bytes over two registers: the upper byte of the first register is address byte 3 and its lower byte is byte 2; the second register holds bytes 1 and 0

registers.name: Subnet mask
registers.description: Same byte layout as the IP address
